title: EKS Private Provisioner Terraform: idempotency, lifecycle hooks, and multi-stage upgrades
creator: Aisha Martinez
description: Implement a production-ready Terraform module to provision Redwood Private control plane (EKS) into customer VPCs. Goals: ensure idempotent apply behavior across repeated runs, provide pluggable lifecycle/upgrade hooks (canary, drain, rollback), integrate automated cluster health checks, and ship examples and CI integration for safe upgrades and state migrations.
acceptance_criteria: Module can create and upgrade a control-plane EKS cluster into an existing customer VPC using a backed S3/DynamoDB remote state without drift on repeated terraform apply
Upgrade path supports: patch/minor Kubernetes control-plane upgrades and nodegroup replacements with a configurable canary percentage and automated rollback on failed health checks
Health checks emit successes/failures to CloudWatch metric namespace and a synthetic smoke test runs in CI after apply
Module exposes clear inputs/outputs and example composition for: eks-cluster, mgmt IAM roles (cross-account), kms key alias, and nodegroup launch template customization
End-to-end tests exist in infra-ci that exercise create, upgrade (version bump), and destroy flows and complete within CI budget
Documentation + CHANGELOG and upgrade notes are published in the private-deployments repo and a migration guide for existing states is provided
tasks: Design module API: inputs, outputs, provider constraints, and backend requirements
Implement base module: EKS cluster, control-plane config, managed nodegroup template, IAM roles, and required addons
Add lifecycle management hooks: pre_upgrade (canary), post_upgrade (smoke), and on_failure (rollback trigger)
Implement idempotency fixes: avoid non-deterministic tagging, canonicalize timestamps, and stable resource naming
Add health check suite: Kubernetes readiness probes, control-plane metrics, and a small pod-level smoke test that validates API and KV cache behavior
Wire CI pipelines: infra-ci jobs for plan/apply/verify and canary promotion logic
Write documentation: examples, upgrade notes, and troubleshooting guide
Run canary in staging and collect latency/cost/regression metrics before GA
notes: We prefer Terraform module composition over monolith to make upgrades easier for customers that only want control-plane changes
Decision: use AWS EKS managed control plane + managed nodegroups for faster upgrades of control plane; adopt launch templates for custom AMI/AMI patching
Trade-off: managed nodegroups simplify day-2 but limit some low-level tuning (we expose launch template override to mitigate)
State handling: require remote backend (S3 bucket + DynamoDB lock) and document migration steps for teams with local tfstate
KMS: create and reference a customer-scoped KMS alias; module will not create a global key by default to avoid cross-account key sprawl
Provider pinning: recommend >= 5.5 AWS provider; module will include constraints and automated bump PRs from dependabot-style pipeline
Health checks: initial implementation will surface CloudWatch metrics and a Lambda-based alerting bridge; long term we can plug into Console observability dashboards
